commands.review_summary:
The branch changes OpenAI provider normalization so explicit provider-level and per-model `api:"openai-completions"` config can bypass default Responses normalization, and adds a standalone proof script.

PR surface: Source +49, Other +123. Total +172 across 2 files.

Reproducibility: yes. at source/CI level: current main passes configured api values into provider normalization, and PR CI reproduces the introduced lint failure in the added script. I did not run live OpenAI requests in this read-only review.
commands.review_followup: - [P1] No automated repair lane: this PR needs contributor-side real behavior proof, and the small lint repair is secondary to that merge gate.

target.title: fix(openai): respect api:"openai-completions" config in transport normalization (#99273)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Users setting `api: "openai-completions"` at the provider or per-model level for `openai/*` models were silently ignored. The transport was always forced to `"openai-responses"`, causing every `openai/*` call to hang to idle timeout when the user explicitly configured completions mode.

Previous iterations of this PR only fixed the provider-level path. This iteration adds per-model detection — when `api: "openai-completions"` is set on a specific model row (e.g. `models.providers.openai.models: [{id: "gpt-5.5", api: "openai-completions"}]`), it is now also respected.

Fixes #99273.

## Why This Change Was Made

Two independently incorrect things were happening:

1. **`shouldUseOpenAIResponsesTransport`** had a single-char logic bug (`!==` vs `===`) that forced explicit completions config to Responses.

2. **`normalizeOpenAITransport`** shared the same predicate with the transport callback, but models that reach the resolved-model path carry `api: "openai-completions"` as a catalog default — the resolved model's `api` field does not carry provenance. So per-model user config like `{id: "gpt-5.5", api: "openai-completions"}` was indistinguishable from the catalog default `"openai-completions"` after resolution.

The fix has four parts:

1. **`hasExplicitOpenAICompletionsConfig()`** — New helper that checks BOTH `config.models.providers.openai.api` (provider-level) and `config.models.providers.openai.models[].api` (per-model level) to distinguish user intent from catalog defaults.

2. **`normalizeOpenAITransport()`** — Rewritten with its own catalog-normalization logic (checks owner provider + default baseUrl + default api), decoupled from `shouldUseOpenAIResponsesTransport`.

3. **`normalizeResolvedModel` callback** — Checks `hasExplicitOpenAICompletionsConfig` before calling `normalizeOpenAITransport`. When the user explicitly configured completions at either level, returns the model unchanged.

4. **`normalizeTransport` callback** — Checks `hasExplicitOpenAICompletionsConfig` before calling `shouldUseOpenAIResponsesTransport`. When the user explicitly configured completions, returns `undefined` (no override).

**Not modified**: Codex Responses transport hooks, auth profiles, usage tracking, live catalog fetching.

## User Impact

Users who explicitly configure `api: "openai-completions"` at the provider level OR on a specific model row now have their configuration respected. Default behavior for catalog OpenAI models (normalize to Responses) is unchanged.

## Evidence

### Production-code proof — all 3 config levels

Proof script imports the real `buildOpenAIProvider()` and exercises both `normalizeResolvedModel` and `normalizeTransport` callbacks against catalog-default, provider-level, and per-model config scenarios:

```
$ npx tsx scripts/proof-99273-completions-config.mjs

[PASS] resolved: catalog → Responses
[PASS] resolved: provider-level explicit completions  
[PASS] resolved: per-model explicit completions        ← THE FIX (was broken)
[PASS] transport: catalog → Responses
[PASS] transport: provider explicit → undefined
[PASS] transport: per-model explicit → undefined        ← THE FIX (was broken)

6/6 passed
```

### Data flow proof — per-model config survives normalization

```
User config:  {openai: {models: [{id: "gpt-5.5", api: "openai-completions"}]}}
  ↓ model.ts:747-757
  metadataOverrideModel.api = "openai-completions"      (per-model wins)
  resolvedModel.api = "openai-completions"
  ↓ normalizeResolvedModel callback
  hasExplicitOpenAICompletionsConfig(config, "gpt-5.5")
    → openaiCfg.models.some(m => m.id === "gpt-5.5" && m.api === "openai-completions")
    → TRUE → return ctx.model unchanged ✅
```

### Test regression

```
$ npx vitest run extensions/openai/openai-provider.test.ts --run
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  45 passed (45)

$ npx vitest run src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/model.test.ts --run
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  246 passed (246)

$ node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs extensions/openai/openai-provider.ts
→ exit 0
```

### What was not tested

| Not tested | Why acceptable |
|------------|----------------|
| Real OpenAI endpoint E2E for each config level | The proof exercises the exact `normalizeResolvedModel` and `normalizeTransport` callback functions with their real production implementations — the same functions the gateway calls. Whether the API key works beyond this transport-normalization boundary is a separate concern from this predicate fix. |

## Root Cause

Two coupled problems in `extensions/openai/openai-provider.ts`:

1. **`shouldUseOpenAIResponsesTransport`**: A single-character logic error (`!==` for `===`) at L462 caused the early-return guard to execute the opposite of its intended behavior. But fixing this alone broke the transport path's catalog normalization.

2. **`normalizeOpenAITransport`**: Shared the same predicate, creating a coupling where the resolved-model path's catalog normalization and the transport path's per-request override used the same boolean function. After model resolution, the resolved `api` field carries no provenance bit — a per-model `api: "openai-completions"` config and the catalog default `api: "openai-completions"` are identical strings. The only way to distinguish them is to inspect the raw config.

## AI Assistance

AI-assisted. Claude Opus 4.8 (Anthropic). The author understands and takes responsibility for all code changes.
